claims.claim: Basic GTSIO procedures apply except H differences; H fuel and induction fully covered in C-3.
Crank→idler→magnetos; crank→cam cluster→fuel; cam spline→oil/tach; front cam bevel→governor; starter worm→wheel→clutch→shaftgear→crank.

Drive/crank: magnetos 1.5 CW; tach .5 CW; starter 32 CCW (cranking); alternator 3 CW; vacuum/deice/autopilot 1.14 CCW; governor .809 CW. All facing engine drive pad. Propeller .667 CW looking forward.
Adapters, bushings, seals, gears, starter clutch and later H fuel coupling are identified.
Accessory mounting and gearing; fuel delivery; magneto ignition; spring-clutch start; governor function.

limitations: All dimensions, tooth counts/profile, placements, seal details and explosion travel illustrative; no engineering fit or manufacture claim.
Cam 0.5 relationship follows four-stroke cycle; idler speed and fuel gearing chosen for schematic layout, not manufacturer tooth counts.
Governor front drive relocated; actual bevel transfer omitted. Vacuum adapter and H alternator intermediate geometry unresolved; dashed routes are conceptual.
Fuel ratio and fuel direction unverified. Tach ratio is not a separately verified oil-pump specification.
A-4-8 caption calls items 10/11 scavenge gears while narrative uses item 11 for tach; oil/tach naming cross-checked with A-4-16 rather than silently merging labels.
Basic A-3-2 generator pulley wording does not establish H gear-driven alternator transfer geometry.
No IO-520 configuration used; existing IO-520 permold pump remains a separate study.
No accessory detailed internals except referenced drive/clutch parts and schematic pump gear cavities. No flow, oil pressure, wear or failure dynamics.
Historical references do not establish current service applicability; no engine serial number or measured trainer supplied.
Native source solids and rebuild recipe are editable; not a constrained assembly or measured reverse-engineering model.
